story_variants.en:
## Vaathiyaar's Translation Machine

Vaathiyaar stands before a machine with two halves. "The left half (encoder) reads the entire input at once. The right half (decoder) generates the output one token at a time, peeking at the encoder's work. This is the Transformer — the architecture that powers GPT, BERT, and nearly all modern AI."

### Transformer Components

```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import math

class PositionalEncoding(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, d_model, max_len=5000):
        super().__init__()
        pe = torch.zeros(max_len, d_model)
        position = torch.arange(0, max_len).unsqueeze(1).float()
        div_term = torch.exp(torch.arange(0, d_model, 2).float() * -(math.log(10000.0) / d_model))
        pe[:, 0::2] = torch.sin(position * div_term)
        pe[:, 1::2] = torch.cos(position * div_term)
        self.register_buffer('pe', pe.unsqueeze(0))
    
    def forward(self, x):
        return x + self.pe[:, :x.size(1)]

class TransformerBlock(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, d_model, num_heads, d_ff, dropout=0.1):
        super().__init__()
        self.attention = nn.MultiheadAttention(d_model, num_heads, batch_first=True)
        self.norm1 = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        self.ff = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(d_model, d_ff),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(dropout),
            nn.Linear(d_ff, d_model)
        )
        self.norm2 = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout)
    
    def forward(self, x, mask=None):
        # Self-attention + residual + layer norm
        attn_out, _ = self.attention(x, x, x, attn_mask=mask)
        x = self.norm1(x + self.dropout(attn_out))
        # Feed-forward + residual + layer norm
        ff_out = self.ff(x)
        x = self.norm2(x + self.dropout(ff_out))
        return x

class MiniTransformer(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, vocab_size, d_model=128, num_heads=8, num_layers=4, d_ff=512):
        super().__init__()
        self.embedding = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, d_model)
        self.pos_encoding = PositionalEncoding(d_model)
        self.layers = nn.ModuleList([
            TransformerBlock(d_model, num_heads, d_ff) for _ in range(num_layers)
        ])
        self.fc_out = nn.Linear(d_model, vocab_size)
        self.d_model = d_model
    
    def forward(self, x, mask=None):
        x = self.embedding(x) * math.sqrt(self.d_model)
        x = self.pos_encoding(x)
        for layer in self.layers:
            x = layer(x, mask)
        return self.fc_out(x)

model = MiniTransformer(vocab_size=10000)
print(f'Parameters: {sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters()):,}')
```

> **Why Transformers Beat RNNs:** No sequential processing — all tokens processed in parallel. Attention connects any two tokens directly, regardless of distance!
story_variants.ta:
## வாத்தியாரின் மொழிபெயர்ப்பு இயந்திரம்

வாத்தியார் இரண்டு பாதிகள் கொண்ட இயந்திரத்தின் முன் நிற்கிறார். "இடது பாதி (encoder) முழு உள்ளீட்டையும் ஒரே நேரத்தில் படிக்கிறது. வலது பாதி (decoder) ஒரு நேரத்தில் ஒரு token-ஐ உருவாக்குகிறது. இது Transformer — GPT, BERT மற்றும் நவீன AI-ஐ இயக்கும் கட்டமைப்பு."

explanation.en: Positional encoding: sine waves of different frequencies encode token position. Even indices use sin
Odd indices use cos. This gives unique position-dependent patterns the model can learn from
Multi-head self-attention: 8 parallel attention heads each learning different patterns
Layer normalization: normalizes across features (not batch). Stabilizes transformer training
Self-attention: Q=K=V=x. Optional mask for causal (decoder) or padding masking
Residual connection (x + attn_out) followed by layer norm. Same as ResNet idea!
Feed-forward network: expand to 4x dimension then compress back. d_ff is typically 4*d_model
Second residual + norm. Each transformer block: attention+residual+norm, then ff+residual+norm
Scale embeddings by sqrt(d_model) to match positional encoding magnitude

steps.line: for layer in self.layers: x = layer(x, mask)

explanation.en: Stack N transformer blocks. Each refines representations. GPT-3 uses 96 layers!

left.label: RNN/LSTM
left.content:
Sequential processing
O(n) steps for n tokens
Vanishing gradients
Hard to parallelize

right.label: Transformer
right.content:
Parallel processing
O(1) attention connects any two tokens
No vanishing gradients
Highly parallelizable on GPUs

animation_sequence.code:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

# Transformer Encoder Layer
encoder_layer = nn.TransformerEncoderLayer(
    d_model=64, nhead=8, dim_feedforward=256, batch_first=True
)
encoder = nn.TransformerEncoder(encoder_layer, num_layers=2)

x = torch.randn(4, 10, 64)  # batch=4, seq=10, d_model=64
output = encoder(x)
print(f'Input:  {x.shape}')
print(f'Output: {output.shape}')

# Full transformer
transformer = nn.Transformer(d_model=64, nhead=8, num_encoder_layers=2,
                              num_decoder_layers=2, batch_first=True)
src = torch.randn(4, 10, 64)
tgt = torch.randn(4, 5, 64)
out = transformer(src, tgt)
print(f'Transformer output: {out.shape}')

executionSteps.explanation: Stack 2 encoder layers for deeper processing
Batch of 4, sequence length 10, model dim 64
Same shape — self-attention enriches each position with context
Full transformer: encoder + decoder with cross-attention
Output matches target length — decoder attends to encoder output

instruction.en: PyTorch cannot run in this sandbox, so this is the numpy version of what PyTorch does under the hood. Build four parts of a mini Transformer language model. 1) `positional_encoding(seq_len, d_model)`: the sinusoidal table from 'Attention Is All You Need' - PE[pos, 2i] = sin(pos / 10000**(2i/d_model)) and PE[pos, 2i+1] = cos(pos / 10000**(2i/d_model)), shape (seq_len, d_model). 2) `causal_mask(n)`: an n x n boolean matrix, True on and below the diagonal (a token may not look ahead). 3) `layer_norm(x, eps=1e-5)`: normalise each row to mean 0 and variance 1: (x - mean) / sqrt(var + eps) over the last axis. 4) `generate(score_fn, start_ids, steps)`: greedy decoding - starting from a copy of start_ids, append argmax(score_fn(ids)) `steps` times and return the ids. A tiny word-pair model stands in for the trained network.
instruction.ta: இந்த sandbox-ல் PyTorch இயங்காது, எனவே இது PyTorch உள்ளே செய்வதன் numpy பதிப்பு. ஒரு சிறிய Transformer language model-இன் நான்கு பகுதிகளை உருவாக்குங்கள். 1) `positional_encoding(seq_len, d_model)`: 'Attention Is All You Need'-இன் sinusoidal அட்டவணை - PE[pos, 2i] = sin(pos / 10000**(2i/d_model)), PE[pos, 2i+1] = cos(pos / 10000**(2i/d_model)), வடிவம் (seq_len, d_model). 2) `causal_mask(n)`: diagonal-இலும் அதற்குக் கீழும் True உள்ள n x n boolean matrix (ஒரு token முன்னால் பார்க்கக்கூடாது). 3) `layer_norm(x, eps=1e-5)`: ஒவ்வொரு வரிசையையும் mean 0, variance 1 ஆக normalise செய்யுங்கள்: கடைசி axis மீது (x - mean) / sqrt(var + eps). 4) `generate(score_fn, start_ids, steps)`: greedy decoding - start_ids-இன் நகலிலிருந்து தொடங்கி, argmax(score_fn(ids))-ஐ `steps` முறை append செய்து ids-ஐத் திருப்புங்கள். பயிற்சி பெற்ற network-க்குப் பதிலாக ஒரு சிறிய word-pair model பயன்படுகிறது.

practice_challenges.test_code:
import numpy as np
_pe = positional_encoding(5, 4)
assert _pe is not None and np.shape(_pe) == (5, 4), "positional_encoding must have shape (seq_len, d_model)"
assert np.allclose(_pe[0], [0, 1, 0, 1]), "position 0 must be sin(0)=0 on even columns and cos(0)=1 on odd columns"
assert np.allclose(_pe[1], [np.sin(1), np.cos(1), np.sin(1 / 100), np.cos(1 / 100)]), "PE[pos, 2i] = sin(pos / 10000**(2i/d_model)), PE[pos, 2i+1] = cos(...)"
_m = causal_mask(3)
assert _m is not None and np.array_equal(_m, [[True, False, False], [True, True, False], [True, True, True]]), "causal_mask must be True on and below the diagonal"
assert np.asarray(_m).dtype == bool, "causal_mask must be a boolean matrix"
_x = np.array([[1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0], [10.0, 10.0, 10.0, 14.0]])
_ln = layer_norm(_x)
assert _ln is not None and np.allclose(_ln.mean(axis=-1), 0) and np.allclose(_ln.var(axis=-1), 1, atol=1e-3), "each row of layer_norm's output must have mean 0 and variance 1"
assert np.allclose(_ln, (_x - _x.mean(-1, keepdims=True)) / np.sqrt(_x.var(-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-5)), "layer_norm must be (x - mean) / sqrt(var + eps) along the last axis"
_fake = lambda ids: np.eye(5)[(ids[-1] + 1) % 5]
_start = [0]
assert generate(_fake, _start, 3) == [0, 1, 2, 3], "generate must append the argmax token `steps` times"
assert _start == [0], "generate must not modify start_ids"
assert generate(_fake, [3, 4], 2) == [3, 4, 0, 1], "generate must use the last token each step"
print("All transformer tests passed!")

q.en: Why do Transformers need positional encoding?

en: Self-attention has no notion of order; positional encoding adds position information
ta: Self-attention-க்கு வரிசை பற்றிய எண்ணம் இல்லை; positional encoding நிலை தகவலைச் சேர்க்கிறது

q.en: What is the purpose of the feed-forward network in each Transformer block?
q.ta: ஒவ்வொரு Transformer block-லும் feed-forward network-ன் நோக்கம் என்ன?

en: To add non-linear transformation and increase model capacity per position
ta: ஒவ்வொரு நிலையிலும் non-linear transformation மற்றும் மாதிரி திறனை அதிகரிக்க

q.en: What is a causal mask in a decoder Transformer?

en: It prevents each position from attending to future positions
ta: ஒவ்வொரு நிலையும் எதிர்கால நிலைகளுக்கு கவனம் செலுத்துவதைத் தடுக்கிறது

under_the_hood.summary: A transformer is wired from a positional-encoding buffer added to embeddings, an encoder stack that reads the whole source, and a decoder stack that reads the shifted target under a causal mask, attends to the encoder, and ends in a vocabulary layer.

steps.title: Positional encoding as a fixed buffer
steps.body: PositionalEncoding builds a (max_len, d_model) table once. div_term = exp(arange(0, d_model, 2) x -(ln 10000 / d_model)) gives frequencies 1, 1/100 for d_model = 4. Position 5 then gets sin(5) = -0.959 and cos(5) = 0.284 in the fast pair, and sin(0.05) = 0.050 and cos(0.05) = 0.999 in the slow pair. The table is registered as a buffer: saved with the model, never trained.

steps.title: Encoder: read the whole source at once
steps.body: Source tokens are embedded, scaled by sqrt(d_model), added to the positional encoding, and passed through N encoder layers of self-attention plus feed-forward. The result, often called memory, has one d_model-sized vector per source token, each informed by the whole sentence.

steps.title: Decoder input is the target shifted right
steps.body: During training with teacher forcing, the decoder receives '<sos> Je suis' and must predict 'Je suis étudiant': every position predicts the next target token. A square subsequent mask (upper triangle set to -inf) stops position 2 from attending to position 3, so it cannot copy the answer.

props.caption: Causal mask added to decoder attention scores

steps.title: Cross-attention connects the halves
steps.body: Each decoder layer has masked self-attention over the target so far, then cross-attention whose queries come from the decoder and whose keys and values come from the encoder memory, then a feed-forward network. Cross-attention is where the translation 'looks back' at the relevant source words.

nodes.label: cross-attention: Q from decoder, K and V from encoder memory

props.caption: One decoder layer and the output head

steps.title: Inference decodes step by step
steps.body: At inference there is no target to shift. Start with '<sos>', run the decoder, take the most likely (or sampled) next token, append it, and run again until '<eos>' or a length limit. The encoder runs once; the decoder runs once per output token, which is why generation is slower than training.

under_the_hood.takeaway: A transformer is embeddings plus positions, an encoder that reads everything, and a decoder that writes one token at a time under a causal mask while consulting the encoder. Getting the masks and the shift right is most of the implementation work.
